title: Policy Service Desk Reference: Owner Auto Policy Reinstatement Figures
content:
**Owner Auto Policy — reinstatement figures by package.**

| Package | Reinstatement window (calendar days after the cancellation effective date) | Reinstatements with a lapse allowed within one policy term |
|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Point Minimum Limits Liability | 10 | 1 |
| Cardinal Point 50/100/50 Liability | 15 | 1 |
| Cardinal Point 100/200/50 Liability | 15 | 2 |
| Cardinal Point 100/300/50 Liability | 20 | 2 |
| Cardinal Point 100/300/100 Liability | 30 | 2 |
| Cardinal Point 250/500/100 Liability | 30 | 3 |

The reinstatement window is the period during which a policy cancelled for nonpayment may be reinstated with a lapse.

**Figures common to every package.**
- **Statement of No Loss:** a Statement of No Loss signed by the named insured is required before a reinstatement with a lapse.
- **Statement age:** at most 3 calendar days may pass between the date the Statement of No Loss was signed and the date the reinstatement is processed.
- **Postmark receipt:** a mailed payment postmarked on or before the cancellation effective date is treated as received on time if it is received within 10 calendar days after the cancellation effective date.
- **Effective-date offset:** 1 calendar day. The schedule describes this as the days added to the later of the reinstatement payment posting date and the Statement of No Loss signing date, giving the reinstatement effective date, with coverage resuming at 12:01 a.m. that day.

**The two dates the offset is added to.** The payment date read is the posting date of the latest payment posted to the term's billing plan. When the term has more than one plan, the plan entered first is used, and every payment posted on that latest date counts as posted that day. The statement date read is the signing date of the latest Statement of No Loss on the term attesting no loss; when two statements share a signing date, the one entered first is taken. The lapse runs from the cancellation effective date through the day before the reinstatement effective date.

**Hypothetical reading.** Suppose the latest payment posted on the 9th and the Statement of No Loss was signed on the 8th. The later of the two dates is the 9th, so coverage resumes at 12:01 a.m. on the 10th. A lapse that began on the 4th then covers the 4th through the 9th.
